_why: ADR 0165's mutation table, re-derived under scripts/mutate.py.
Two of the three defects in that record are pure Python and live here.
The third -- the unterminated JSX comment in CliApp.tsx -- is NOT in this
set, and its absence is deliberate. Grading it means running
`pnpm run typecheck`, which needs the Node toolchain and a completed pnpm
install; a set file that shelled out to pnpm would report NOT CAUGHT on
every machine that had not run one, which is the confident-wrong answer
mutate.py exists to prevent. It was verified by hand instead, by restoring
the byte that caused it, and the ADR records the exact compiler error and
says this is where the evidence is weaker.
test: cd Tests && python3 -m pytest test_runner_contract.py test_lab_report.py --no-header -p no:cacheprovider

mutations.description: the runner resolves a taxon id and then emits null instead
mutations._note: The house defect -- computed and not delivered. Before this pass no test in the file could see it: every other test ran with the NCBI lookup returning nothing, so null was the expected output everywhere and deleting the two assignments changed nothing any assertion looked at.

mutations.description: the report leaves the refusals section blank instead of stating that nothing was withheld
mutations._note: The branch this mutates was unreachable from the suite before this pass: the shared report() fixture now carries a source-mixture refusal, so every test that built a report exercised the OTHER branch, and the test named for this one was asserting the no-refusal sentence against a document that had a refusal in it.
mutations.find:
"Nothing was withheld: every parameter resolved to a cited value "
            "or was supplied by you.",
